error_chain: Flask's globals.py defines `request` as a LocalProxy backed by werkzeug.local.Local with a contextvars-based storage strategy
Werkzeug's local.py replaced the threadlocal storage with contextvars.ContextVar so that async coroutines see a per-task logical context
Flask's ctx.py pushes a RequestContext onto the Local stack at the start of dispatching and pops it at request teardown
When the async view awaits asyncio.create_task(coro), the task captures the current context via copy_context, preserving the bound request proxy

When code instead schedules work onto a thread pool or uses a bare ensure_future without copying context, the spawned task evaluates ContextVar.get() in an empty context, raising RuntimeError from the LocalProxy access
trigger_conditions: Customer code awaits a coroutine via run_in_executor or thread-pool worker which does not propagate the active contextvars context
Werkzeug's Local switched from threadlocal to ContextVar storage, so the regression appeared after the werkzeug 2.0+ upgrade
Flask's RequestContext proxy raises RuntimeError when the underlying ContextVar.get() returns LookupError, masking the contextvars cause

expected_answer.error_origin: werkzeug.local.Local's ContextVar storage returns LookupError in the spawned task because the parent context was not copied at task creation
expected_answer.bypass_reason: asyncio.create_task captures the current context but ensure_future from a thread pool or run_in_executor does not, so the LocalProxy resolves to an empty contextvars binding
expected_answer.correct_config: Use loop.run_in_executor with contextvars.copy_context().run, or push a Flask app/request context inside the coroutine via app.test_request_context() / app.app_context() so the proxy resolves before any thread-pool offload
